transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-21
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~49 minutes
Location: Zoom (recording)
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Oliver Reed (Suncrest Head of Platform), Nadia Alvarez (Suncrest CISO), Priya Desai (Suncrest ML Engineer)

Summary (auto):
Quick discovery focused on crypto key residency requirements, KMS/HSM constraints, log sanitization and retention policies for financial services. Suncrest is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; primary concern is proof that keys and plain text logs are never stored in non-EU regions and that audit logs can be shimmed into their security lake.

Topics:
- Key residency / KMS / HSM options
- Logging: raw transcripts, PII redaction, audit log routing and retention
- Deployment: private control plane vs dedicated GPUs vs fully hosted
- Compliance controls: GDPR data subject requests, HIPAA boundaries for health-adjacent employee data, SOC2 evidence generation

Action items (captured live): see metadata above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Ethan Park: Hey thanks for making time everyone, I'll kick off quick — Ethan from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account, and with me is Maya Chen our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Oliver Reed: Hey Ethan, hi Maya, Oliver here. Thanks — we've got Nadia and Priya on the line; Nadia is our CISO taking point on controls, and Priya runs the models and will own the POC.
[00:18] Nadia Alvarez: Hi all. Quick note, we have a hard requirement: customer crypto keys (KMS/HSM) for production must remain under EU law, like an EU tenancy or on-prem HSM. Also logs containing any sort of identified customer data must never egress to US regions.
[00:31] Maya Chen: Understood — thanks for putting that up front. We recently worked with a bis-uh, bank, on a similar constraint. To confirm, is the ask that Redwood never see raw keys and that log storage must be region-locked to EU?
[00:44] Nadia Alvarez: Exactly. Also, we need the ability to rotate keys on our schedule and be able to bring our own key material (BYOK).
[00:52] Priya Desai: From ML side, we also need KV cache persistence choices — we'd rather not have any prefix cache written to centralized logs, or if it is, it needs to be redacted.
[01:03] Ethan Park: Right. High level: we offer Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. For your constraints, Private deployment gives the strongest guarantees — private control plane running in your VPC or on-prem, and KMS integration with customer-owned HSMs. Dedicated can also be region-restricted but keys typically live in the cloud provider KMS accessible to the Redwood node; we can discuss an HSM passthrough.
[01:19] Oliver Reed: Can you give more detail on passthrough? In other vendors it's often more of a KMS-style API call, but we need to know root of trust stays with us.
[01:27] Maya Chen: Sure — for Private, the Redwood agent runs in your VPC and we don't store keys in our control plane. The runtime will request ephemeral session keys via your KMS/HSM using a transient credential. We can provide an architecture diagram, I can point you to our HSM integration notes.
[01:40] Nadia Alvarez: Important: audit logs must show key access events, and also model input/output events must be kept separate from operator logs. We will be ingesting audit events into our security lake.
[01:50] Maya Chen: We have an audit-forwarding hook — it can stream structured events to your syslog/Kafka/S3 endpoint. Note there is often a tradeoff on verbosity; we can redact payloads. We also publish per-request metadata like model id, token counts, latencies.
[02:06] Priya Desai: On redaction, is there a built-in PII scrubber? We do some post-processing but ideally we'd like server-side scrubbing before anything leaves the host.
[02:15] Maya Chen: We have a sanitization plug-in that can apply regex and ML-based PII redaction before logs are forwarded. Caveat: more aggressive redaction can impact debugging. It's configurable per-route.
[02:27] Oliver Reed: What's the data path? I want to be absolutely clear: if we use Redwood Hosted, do transcripts cross into US infra at any point?
[02:35] Ethan Park: For Hosted, we have regions. EU-hosted endpoints keep customer payloads in EU by default, but some telemetry and aggregated metrics may traverse our analytics pipeline which sits in US — we can opt you out of that pipeline for enterprise agreements. For regulated customers we usually recommend Dedicated or Private to get contractual controls.
[02:53] Nadia Alvarez: Contract is one thing; we also need to ensure logs are scrubbed and never stored unencrypted. If Redwood's debugging requires snapshotting, we need a process to request and review and explicit consent.
[03:05] Maya Chen: Agreed; we have a debug snapshot workflow where snapshots are ephemeral, stored in customer region, and only created with signed approvals. We can include the policy doc.
[03:13] Priya Desai: Another practical question — in the model serving path, does Redwood ever persist plain-text prompts or completions to disk outside customer-specified storage?
[03:21] Maya Chen: No persistence in the control plane for Private. In Dedicated, ephemeral nodes may use local disk for caching; those disks are encrypted and wiped on instance termination. For Hosted, we persist short-term caches for performance and may persist anonymized traces by default — but for enterprise you can opt out.
[03:40] Oliver Reed: How about data subject requests? Under GDPR, we may need to present deletion or export of prompt histories. Can we get a mapping of what logs need to be deleted and how Redwood supports that?
[03:50] Ethan Park: Yes — we support DSAR workflows: we can map identifiers to events and delete or export depending on retention. We'll need to confirm what metadata you plan to capture to link to subjects.
[03:59] Nadia Alvarez: On HIPAA — it's not our primary posture but we do process some health-adjacent employee benefits data in Europe. Is Redwood willing to sign a BAA for EU processing?
[04:10] Maya Chen: We have customers processing PHI in US and EU. We can discuss HIPAA/BAA terms — generally that's easier on Dedicated/Private deployments. I'll flag that and pull in our compliance team if needed.
[04:20] Priya Desai: For the POC we will want to compare latency and cost between a Private in our Azure EU region and Redwood Dedicated in eu-west-1. Can Redwood run a bench that mirrors our typical prompt lengths (avg 800 tokens) and concurrency (30 qps)?
[04:33] Ethan Park: Absolutely. Maya, we'll schedule a perf bench with their sample prompts — note that 800 tokens and 30 qps is heavy on KV cache and batching; might affect cost.
[04:42] Maya Chen: For that workload we often recommend a medium-size quantized model and enable prefix/KV caching. We can give recommended autoscaling and batch sizes. Priya, can you provide a sample prompt corpus and the expected latency SLO?
[04:55] Priya Desai: Our SLO is p95 < 350ms for short-turn queries but for these longer ones we are comfortable with p95 < 1s. We'll send prometheus traces after initial run.
[05:06] Oliver Reed: One more — keys. We run a Thales HSM on-prem; we'd like a direct HSM connection or bring-your-own-key via EKMI. Is Redwood compatible?
[05:16] Maya Chen: We have customers using HSMs via a PKCS#11 bridge and via cloud HSM passthrough. For on-prem Thales we can route calls through a private connector; for production we typically recommend Private deployment to avoid extra network hops.
[05:29] Nadia Alvarez: We also need tamper-evident logs for audit. Do you support signed audit trails?
[05:35] Maya Chen: We do sign certain audit events and can provide integrity proofs (HMAC) and support streaming to your Immutable S3 or WORM storage. We'll need to work through retention windows and legal hold.
[05:47] Priya Desai: Regarding logs that contain tokens: we need explicit token redaction and the ability to truncate the first N tokens for model-input persistence. Can that be per-route?
[05:58] Maya Chen: Yes per-route. You can set redaction rules and a TTL for stored prompts and completions. We also support token-level masking if you want to never persist certain spans.
[06:09] Oliver Reed: Will you put this in writing — a little architecture + controls appendix — so our audit team can review?
[06:14] Ethan Park: Yes we'll share an architecture diagram and a controls appendix. I'll add SOC2/HIPAA mapping and the HSM integration notes.
[06:21] Nadia Alvarez: For the POC we want strict settings: all logs to EU S3, KMS BYOK with on-prem HSM, debug snapshots disabled except on request, and signed audit trails. If Redwood can demonstrate that in the bench we'll move forward.
[06:33] Maya Chen: Sounds good. Just to manage expectations, the Private deployment will require network configuration and a short onboarding window; Dedicated is faster to start but may need add'l contract language for BYOK/HSM.
[06:45] Priya Desai: On timelines — we hope to have a vendor decision by end of September. The POC should start early Sept.
[06:53] Ethan Park: We'll align on dates in the follow-up. We'll target a bench the week of Aug 31 and a Private deployment onboarding slated for early Sept if all goes well.
[07:01] Oliver Reed: Cool. A couple of random clarifications: will debug / support teams at Redwood ever be able to see redacted payloads?
[07:08] Maya Chen: By default support has access only to metadata. Any access to payloads is gated by the debug snapshot workflow and audited. For enterprise agreements we can require two-person approvals.
[07:18] Nadia Alvarez: Also need to confirm the incident response playbook if a key is suspected compromised — how do you revoke sessions and rotate keys gracefully?
[07:27] Ethan Park: The runtime supports key rotation via short-lived session keys; we can revoke active sessions and force rekey. We'll provide an IR playbook excerpt in the docs.
[07:36] Priya Desai: We will test a simulated key-rotation scenario during the POC.
[07:40] Maya Chen: Great — we'll add that to the perf bench plan.
[07:44] Ethan Park: Ok, wrapping up — quick recap of next steps: Ethan send architecture diagram and private deployment notes; Maya send SOC2/HIPAA controls mapping and HSM integration doc; Priya send sample prompt corpus and redaction spec. We'll schedule perf bench week of Aug 31.
[07:58] Oliver Reed: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[08:01] Nadia Alvarez: Thanks — we'll await the docs.
[08:03] Priya Desai: Thanks all.

(End of recording)

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-hearings — e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "K-V cash" in a couple spots; some speaker attribution inconsistent early in the call.
